items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And that was like musicians from Basie, Cab Calloway, Ellington, Les Brown, Jimmie Lunceford, and all these musicians was out there.

ctx.x: Yes. You told me of some of the places and people that you performed with before you met Count Basie. Start us there and bring us into your time with Count Basie.

Well that’d be wonderful. I start back in the United States Navy. And as you know it was a long time before the blacks could enter the United States Navy, and when this came about I was still in school and I says well I know they’re getting ready to draft me into the Army so before they draft me into the Army I will shoot for the Navy. So coming out of the of the Pottstown High School, in which I had played all the marches and played with the school dance band, but I played tuba, see. Because we didn’t have any…

was that when the Great Lakes football team would play, you’d have that privilege of going to the games with the bugle and drum corps, see? And that was a treat because that’s where they had Otto and Martin Graham and all those great football players that had come out of the various different schools. And from there I would try to play trombone because the tuba had become obsolete, where the tuba had went out. There was no more tuba playing in which it’s coming back today again. It’s that cycle going around.
